title: PLD for recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer
schedule_label: One infusion on day 1 of each 28-day cycle. Six cycles are typical. Your consultant may continue treatment while it helps and side effects remain manageable.
schedule_summary: One infusion on day 1 of each 28-day cycle. Six cycles are typical. Your consultant may continue treatment while it helps and side effects remain manageable.
purpose: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is being offered to slow the growth of recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer. Your team will review symptoms and scan results with you to decide whether to continue.
administration_text: The team uses the pegylated liposomal formulation and starts the first infusion slowly. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest tightness, back pain or breathing difficulty.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, ECG and an echo or MUGA scan to measure heart function. Before each cycle: blood count, kidney and liver tests. The team also monitors ECG, hand–foot symptoms and mouth sores. Repeat heart imaging depends on symptoms and cumulative exposure. Symptoms and imaging according to your consultant’s plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin is carried inside tiny coated fat particles called liposomes. This changes how it circulates and its side-effect pattern. Heart injury remains possible; skin and mouth effects are especially important.
agents.watch: Report painful palms / soles or mouth ulcers early. Keep heart-test appointments and report breathlessness, swelling or chest symptoms; tell staff immediately about an infusion reaction.
risks: Mouth soreness or ulcers affecting eating and drinking
Low blood counts, infection, fatigue and nausea
Heart damage and infusion reactions; risk depends partly on previous treatment
consent_risks: Tender red palms or soles can peel or blister. Ring before skin pain limits walking or everyday tasks.
Mouth ulcers, nausea and poor appetite can limit drinking. Contact the team early for pain relief and mouth care.
Call immediately for fever, chills, bleeding or sudden illness.
Report increasing breathlessness, swollen ankles or chest pain. Heart checks guide further doses.
Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest tightness or burning around the cannula.

consent_support: Recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer. Discuss expected benefit, alternatives, side effects and the option of symptom-directed care. Record the individual decision and any off-label discussion. Endometrial cancer is listed by NCCP and falls outside the licensed indications for Caelyx. Explain and document this according to local policy.

evidence.title: GOG phase II study of PLD in previously treated endometrial cancer
evidence.interpretation: Some participants with persistent or recurrent endometrial cancer had a partial response to PLD.
evidence.limitations: This small single-arm study cannot establish a survival advantage or predict an individual response.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.timing: Up to three times daily if needed; at least 6 hours apart. Maximum 30 mg or 0.5 mg/kg per day, whichever is lower, for up to 5 days.

prescription_notes: Reconcile rescue medicines across the cycle. Use only one metoclopramide prescription; check kidney function and contraindications.

local_adjuncts.directions: Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
